newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania c.bank governor says 1997 inflation higher.
newsitem.headline: Romania c.bank governor says 1997 inflation higher.

text.p: Romanian central bank governor Romania's Mugur Isarescu revised lower a forecast for 1997 year-on-year inflation to up 89.5 percent from last year's 56.9 percent.
Isarescu's forecast, issued at a news conference, was lower than Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea's government forecast last week of 97 percent.

Isarescu said his forecast was included in the letter of intent that the government sent to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in Washington following a month of negotiations in Bucharest on resuming credits to the Balkan country.

Isarescu also said Romania had pledged to cut the consolidated budget deficit, including the "BNR's quasifiscal subsidies", to 4.5 percent of gross domestic product this year from last year's 6.5 percent.

Ciorbea also said last week that his centrist coalition government sought a reduction to 4.5 percent. But his calculation of last year's deficit of 5.8 percent did not include the central bank's "quasifiscal subsidies" to the farming sector, due to be phased out this year.
Last year, the former leftist government obliged the BNR to subsidise the farming sector through cheap loans, which at end-1996 accounted for 16 percent of its overall refinancing.
The consolidated budget gap includes the central budget, local budgets, social security budget and other funds.
Isarescu said final forecasts for macroeconomic indicators would be available after the IMF analysed Bucharest's proposals under the letter of intent. He gave no further details.

He said the main focus of the government package presented by Ciorbea this week was to cut monthly inflation to around 2.0 percent in the final months of 1997, through steps to reduce the budget and current account deficits.
Isarescu said a sharp rise in consumer prices in the first quarter was a temporary blip triggered by liberalisation of fuel, electicity and food prices.
Latest data showed monthly inflation climbed to 13.7 percent in January from 10.3 percent last December. January data on the budget deficit was not yet available.
